title: Musculoskeletal, breast, obstetric and paediatric anatomy

steps.tx: The **Rotator cuff** muscular envelope stabilizes the glenohumeral joint. It comprises the subscapularis (anteriorly inserting into the lesser tuberosity), the **supraspinatus** (superiorly inserting into the superior facet of the greater tuberosity), the infraspinatus (posteriorly inserting into the middle facet), and the teres minor (inferiorly into the inferior facet).
steps.say: The Rotator cuff muscular envelope stabilizes the glenohumeral joint. rows: Middle facet of greater tuberosity (external rotator)
Inferior facet of greater tuberosity (external rotator)

steps.tx: The **Carpal tunnel** is an inelastic osteofibrous canal bounded by carpal bones deeply and the flexor retinaculum superficially. The canal transmits exactly 9 flexor tendons (4 flexor digitorum superficialis, 4 flexor digitorum profundus, and 1 flexor pollicis longus) and the **median nerve**, which lies directly beneath the retinaculum vulnerable to compression neuropathy.

points: Ulnar nerve and artery (within Guyon canal)

steps.tx: The wrist carpus comprises 8 bones in 2 transverse rows: proximal row (scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform) and distal row (trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate). The **scaphoid** blood supply enters retrograde via distal capsular branches, predisposing waist fractures to delayed union and **avascular necrosis** of the proximal pole.
steps.say: The wrist carpus comprises 8 bones in 2 transverse rows: proximal row of scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, and pisiform, and distal row of trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, and hamate. The scaphoid blood supply enters retrograde via distal capsular branches, predisposing waist fractures to delayed union and avascular necrosis of the proximal pole.

rows: Intercalated segment; scaphoid and lunate articulate with radius
Rigid transverse arch articulating with metacarpal bases
Proximal pole isolated upon fracture, leading to osteonecrosis

steps.tx: Knee stability relies on cruciate and collateral ligaments with precise condylar attachments. The **anterior cruciate ligament** originates from the posteromedial aspect of the lateral femoral condyle, inserting on the anterior tibial intercondylar area. Conversely, the **posterior cruciate ligament** originates from the anterolateral aspect of the medial femoral condyle.

left.title: Anterior Cruciate Ligament (ACL)
points: Origin: Posteromedial aspect of lateral femoral condyle
Prevents anterior tibial translation and internal rotation
Consists of anteromedial and posterolateral bundles

right.title: Posterior Cruciate Ligament (PCL)
points: Origin: Anterolateral aspect of medial femoral condyle
Consists of anterolateral and posteromedial bundles
Torn with direct anterior tibial dashboard impact

steps.tx: Paediatric elbow secondary ossification centres appear in chronological order remembered by the **CRITOE** mnemonic: **Capitellum** at 1 year, Radial head at 3 years, Internal (medial) epicondyle at 5 years, Trochlea at 7 years, Olecranon at 9 years, and External (lateral) epicondyle at 11 years.
steps.say: Paediatric elbow secondary ossification centres appear in chronological order remembered by the CRITOE mnemonic: Capitellum at 1 year, Radial head at 3 years, Internal or medial epicondyle at 5 years, Trochlea at 7 years, Olecranon at 9 years, and External or lateral epicondyle at 11 years.

steps.tx: **Axillary lymph node** staging for breast carcinoma is anatomically categorized relative to the **pectoralis minor** muscle: Level 1 nodes lie lateral and inferior to pectoralis minor, Level 2 nodes lie directly posterior to pectoralis minor, and Level 3 nodes lie medial and superior to pectoralis minor beneath the subclavius.

left.title: Axillary Node Levels
points: Level 1: Lateral and inferior to pectoralis minor
Level 2: Deep and posterior to pectoralis minor
Level 3: Medial and superior to pectoralis minor

right.title: Internal Mammary Chain
points: Important in medial and central breast tumors
Evaluated on cross-sectional CT and MRI

steps.tx: The **Terminal ductal lobular unit** (TDLU) represents the functional milk-producing unit of the female breast, comprising an extralobular terminal duct and acinar ductules. The TDLU is the histopathological and radiological origin of almost all breast neoplasms, including both invasive ductal and lobular carcinomas as well as benign **fibroadenomas** and cysts.

rows: Ductal carcinoma, lobular carcinoma, fibroadenoma, cysts
Intraductal papilloma, duct ectasia, periductal mastitis

steps.tx: Antenatal obstetric ultrasound evaluates the normal fetal **umbilical cord**, identifying 3 vessels surrounded by gelatinous **Wharton jelly**: 2 umbilical arteries carrying deoxygenated blood from the fetus to the placenta, and 1 umbilical vein carrying oxygenated blood from the placenta to the fetus. Single umbilical artery occurs in 1% of pregnancies, prompting detailed fetal anatomical surveys.

left.title: Normal 3-Vessel Cord
points: Classic Mickey Mouse sign on axial sonogram

right.title: Single Umbilical Artery (SUA)
points: Agenesis or atrophy of one umbilical artery
Found in approximately 1% of singleton gestations
Associated with renal and cardiovascular anomalies
Increased risk of intrauterine growth restriction
Indicates fetal echocardiography and detailed survey
